claims.text: Every artifact that bears on this trip describes one and the same trip: EV-TRIP-00519, EV-GPS-00519 and EV-FARE-00519 all carry trip_id TRP-00519, the trace's first fix at 08:06:40+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at, and all three are admitted at weight_multiplier 1.0 with an empty issues list. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 as to identity is therefore discharged, and no admitted artifact contradicts her account of the ride.

The rider's route instruction satisfies POL-RD-04 on its face. It came from the rider (limb (a)); it was sent at 08:08:10+08:00, ninety seconds after the trip started at 08:06:40+08:00, so it precedes any departure from the corridor (limb (b)); and it does not say 'go the fast way' or 'you know better' — it names roads, 'take Clementi Rd then North Buona Vista', which is specific enough to act on (limb (c)). It is exactly the kind of instruction the clause treats as actionable, not a vague passenger wish the driver may brush aside.

The driver's silence is carried by an artifact, not by assertion. EV-CHAT-00519 records exactly two messages for the whole trip, both from the rider — MSG-00519-001 at 08:08:10 and MSG-00519-002 'hello?' at 08:10:40 — each marked delivered and read before the next was sent, and not one message from the driver, in a chat the trip_record confirms ran to two messages. Any account that cites no artifact to the contrary carries no weight under POL-RD-08, so the rider's account that the driver refused to explain or discuss is the only account of the exchange on the record.

POL-RD-01 makes the trace the governing measurement, and on EV-GPS-00519 the vehicle covered 2.71 km against a booked optimal of 5.0 km — an excess of -2.29 km, derived excess_pct -45.8%, derived status 'no deviation'. The rider therefore does not press a POL-RD-02 distance recomputation, which on these numbers would yield nothing; her case is that she received roughly 46% less of the booked journey than she was charged for, after her written instruction was left unanswered.

Nothing in the pool can exculpate the driver's route choice. The only traffic advisory linked to this trip, EV-ADVIS-00519-01, is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, blocking issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, detail 'No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window' — and that impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02 requires. Under POL-GEN-02(3) the absence is itself citable while it can carry no fact, and under POL-RD-03 an advisory that does not exist cannot exculpate any corridor decision; so no closure, contraflow or other external event explains the route or the silence.

The rider is not the claimant POL-RD-08 guards against: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the enhanced-corroboration condition (four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated) is not engaged and no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required of her. These are the two profile fields POL-RD-08 names and they are cited for that test alone, as POL-GEN-01 requires; no other profile field on either party is relied on here.

With fare_breakdown.payment_status at CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd at 0.00 (EV-FARE-00519), a NO_ACTION leaves the rider carrying the entire disputed 9.99 for a trip whose central question — whether the driver's route and his refusal to answer a plainly stated instruction were justified — rests on nothing the record can test: the sole advisory is absent at weight 0.0, chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, and no road-level fact is derived from the trace. That is the situation POL-RD-10 addresses, and its limb (7) applies: the two accounts are of comparable strength and the deciding fact is carried by no artifact. The rider asks that the amount be held for human review rather than collected from her — under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held, not collected, and under POL-RD-10 the rider is not left paying in full on an unanswered record.

The trip did not deviate: the governing gps_trace measures the route at 2.71 km against an optimal route of 5.0 km, an excess of −2.29 km (−45.8%). Because the excess is negative, neither POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms) can pass, and POL-RD-01 directs that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and this trace is whole: 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps listed and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs (a gap over 90 s, a jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 s) is met. The trace is unimpaired and its 2.71 km figure governs over the rounded 2.7 km convenience copy on the trip_record.

The only reason the distance driven is below the optimal 5.0 km is the rider's own election to end the trip: the trip_record dropoff is labelled 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early' and the trip ended at 08:18:40. A journey cut short by the passenger produces a shortfall, not an excess, and POL-RD-01 measures only excess over the optimal route.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 to show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The only trace in the bundle shows a negative excess, so the burden is not discharged, the burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause needs to be reached at all.

Even on the fare arithmetic there is nothing to refund: the POL-RD-02 recomputed optimal-route fare is SGD 10.87 against a charged total of SGD 9.99, so charged_total minus recomputed_fare is negative, the refund floors at zero, and it is below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis line in any event. The rider in fact paid less than the optimal route would have cost.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction to add: the fare_breakdown shows no ERP gantries (erp_lines empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00) and no promo or toll lines, so the standalone ERP and surcharge refunds available under POL-RD-09 (including limb (4)) are unavailable and nothing can be added on top of a zero distance refund.

The rider's real complaint is the driver's silence, not distance: the chat log contains only two messages, both from the rider (a route preference at 08:08:10 and 'hello?' at 08:10:40), and neither records anything bearing on a distance excess. A communication grievance is not a route deviation and raises no monetary remedy under this policy; the dispute remains governed by the POL-RD-01 threshold, which the trip fails to cross.

The outcome for this rider-filed dispute follows POL-GEN-03: with no deviation established the ruling is NO_ACTION, which leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they stand. The rider's request for a full refund of the SGD 9.99 is not supported by the evidence and the present payment state is preserved.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this is a route-deviation dispute, and on the route the evidence does not support a refund.

No deviation. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement. EV-GPS-00519 (weight 1.0) is complete and unimpaired: 73 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, so none of the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) impairment limbs is met. Its trace distance is 2.71 km against a booked optimal of 5.0 km (EV-TRIP-00519). The excess is 2.71 - 5.0 = -2.29 km (-45.8%), i.e. below the optimal, not above it. Neither establishment test passes (not greater than 0.8 km, not greater than 20% of optimal), so POL-RD-01 gives NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised.

Why the distance is short. The trip record itself records the dropoff as 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early'. A journey cut short by the passenger produces a shortfall, not an excess. The fare confirms it: the rider was charged SGD 9.99 (base 3.80 + distance 2.03 + time 3.36 + platform fee 0.80) for 2.7 km, while a full optimal-route trip recomputes under POL-RD-02 to SGD 10.87. She paid less than the optimal route would have cost, so a POL-RD-02 recomputation refunds nothing (charged_total 9.99 - recomputed_fare 10.87 is negative and floors at zero, below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis line in any event).

On the instruction and the silence. The rider is right that the driver did not reply: EV-CHAT-00519 contains exactly two messages, both from her (the route suggestion at 08:08:10 and 'hello?' at 08:10:40), and the driver's account that he followed the app route and she chose to get out is consistent with the trace. But a communication grievance is not a route deviation and carries no monetary remedy under this policy. The rider's POL-RD-04 point is answered: with no excess there is nothing for exoneration to exclude, and the clause's corroboration test could not be run in any event because chat_message.waypoint_hint is null and no road-level fact is derived from the trace. The rider's POL-RD-03 point is also answered: the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00519-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); its absence is citable but it carries no fact, and no closure is asserted by either side, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing.

No other route to money. There is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09: the fare breakdown shows no ERP gantries (erp_lines empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge, no promo or toll lines. No POL-RD-06 referral fires: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and no material deviation is recorded. No POL-RD-04 driver compensation is due: the distance charged (2.7 km) matches the trace (2.71 km), a shortfall of 0.01 km, far under the 1.0 km trigger.

Nothing in POL-RD-10 escalates this: the trip identifiers all match TRP-00519, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, and no charge line is unmatched. The rider's identity showing (POL-RD-08) and her profile point (her deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so no enhanced corroboration applies) are accepted but do not change the outcome.

The present state therefore stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left as they are, and the SGD 9.99 charge is neither reversed nor held.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The charge of SGD 9.99 stands and is not refunded.

Why there is no route deviation. POL-RD-01 measures excess as actual distance minus the optimal route, and the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km. EV-GPS-00519 records 2.71 km driven; the booked optimal route was 5.0 km (EV-TRIP-00519). The excess is therefore -2.29 km, or -45.8% (the trace-derived status is 'no deviation'). POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH more than 20% of the optimal route AND more than 0.8 km. Neither test is met, because the ride was shorter than the optimal route, not longer. The reason is on the trip record itself: the dropoff is labelled 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early' — the rider ended the journey before the booked destination, which produces a shortfall, not an excess. POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either establishment test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

For completeness on the money. POL-RD-02 does not run at all without an established deviation. Even if it were run, its arithmetic (base fare SGD 3.80 + 0.75 x 5.0 km + 0.28 x 9 min = SGD 10.07, times the surge multiplier 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown EV-FARE-00519, plus the SGD 0.80 platform fee = SGD 10.87) exceeds the SGD 9.99 charged, so charged_total minus recomputed_fare is negative, the refund floors at zero and is below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis line in any event. The rider in fact paid less than the optimal route would have cost, and she was billed only for the 2.7 km she rode (base 3.80 + distance 2.03 + time 3.36 + platform fee 0.80 = 9.99); she is not charged for the portion she chose not to take.

No pass-through or billing-integrity correction. EV-FARE-00519 shows no ERP gantries (erp_lines empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00) and no promo, so the standalone corrections available under POL-RD-09, including limb (4), are unavailable: there is no phantom line and nothing to add.

For the rider. Your written instruction — 'take Clementi Rd then North Buona Vista, fewer lights', sent 08:08:10 — is recorded in the chat log, and I accept your account that the driver did not reply: EV-CHAT-00519 carries exactly two messages, both yours (the second 'hello?' at 08:10:40), each marked delivered and read, and the driver's statement confirms he kept to the app. But POL-RD-04 exonerates a rider-requested detour against a deviation that has been established, and there is no deviation here to exonerate; its waypoint_hint is also null on both messages, so its corroboration test could not be run. A driver's failure to communicate is not itself a route deviation, and no clause in this policy attaches money to it. Driver-conduct review under POL-RD-06(c) is a referral only where a repeat-deviation pattern is established on the named counters — deviation_flags_90d of 3 or more, or 5% of at least 40 completed 90-day trips — and EV-DPROF-00519 shows 0 of 250, so no referral fires and no pattern may be used to establish a deviation on this trip.

On the missing advisory. EV-ADVIS-00519-01 carries weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence is citable but it can carry no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)). No party has asserted a closure, so nothing turns on it. The driver's assertion that he followed the app route is consistent with the trace and is accepted.

Why this does not escalate. The trace is whole: 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, so none of the POL-RD-07(a)–(c) impairment limbs is met and no POL-RD-10(3) or POL-RD-10(1) trigger applies. The trip identifiers on the trip record, trace and fare breakdown all agree (TRP-00519) and their timestamps are consistent, no charge line is unmatched, and the computed refund does not exceed the ceiling. My confidence in this ruling is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.

Outcome. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is NO_ACTION: fare_breakdown.payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00, exactly as they stand. The disputed SGD 9.99 is neither refunded nor held; no driver compensation and no referral arise.

The route-deviation test in POL-RD-01 compares the distance actually driven with the booked optimal route. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00519, weight 1.0): 2.71 km against a booked optimal of 5.0 km (EV-TRIP-00519, weight 1.0). That is an excess of -2.29 km (-45.8%) — a shortfall, not an excess. Both establishment tests require an excess greater than 20% of the optimal route AND greater than 0.8 km; neither can pass on a negative figure. No deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip felt to the rider.

The trace is whole — 73 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) impairment limbs are not met and the 2.71 km trace figure governs over the rounded 2.7 km convenience copy on the trip record.

The fare arithmetic points the same way. Recomputed on the booked optimal route under POL-RD-02, the fare would be SGD 10.87 (base SGD 3.80 + 0.75 × 5.0 km + 0.28 × 9 min + SGD 0.80 platform fee) against SGD 9.99 actually charged, so the refund floors at zero and is de minimis in any event: the rider paid less than the optimal route would have cost. There are no ERP gantry lines and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 yields no separate pass-through or billing-integrity correction, and nothing can be added to a zero distance refund.

The rider's request for a full refund rests on the driver's silence. I accept the account in EV-CHAT-00519: two rider messages (08:08:10 asking for Clementi Rd and North Buona Vista, and 08:10:40 'hello?'), delivered and read, with no reply from the driver, consistent with EV-TRIP-00519's chat_message_count of 2. I also accept the rider's POL-RD-04 point that the instruction was specific enough to act on. But a communication grievance is not a route deviation, and this policy attaches no money to it in this category; and because the rider alighted early, no excess distance exists for POL-RD-04 to exonerate. No driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04 either: the fare billed 2.7 km against a 2.71 km trace, a shortfall of 0.01 km, far below the 1.0 km threshold.

On the driver's side, the identity and burden points under POL-RD-08 are accepted (all artifacts carry TRP-00519, and no excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold from the unimpaired trace), and the POL-RD-01/POL-RD-07 trace-integrity point is accepted. The only traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00519-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); its absence cannot exculpate any corridor decision, and nothing turns on it because no deviation exists. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged — there is no material deviation and no pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips in 90 days) — so no driver-conduct referral arises. The rider-profile fields cited under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0) do not engage enhanced corroboration.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. POL-GEN-03 leaves the present state as it is — payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are unchanged. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trace is unimpaired, all identifiers and timestamps on the admitted artifacts agree, the exculpatory clauses are not invoked against anything missing, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. Confidence rests on the deciding facts being carried by artifacts at full weight (EV-GPS-00519, EV-TRIP-00519, EV-FARE-00519, all 1.0). If the rider wants the driver's non-response reviewed as a service-quality matter, that is a legitimate concern but it is not a matter this category's money rules address, and no clause here produces a referral for it.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the central fact, and the record confirms it: the vehicle did not travel a longer route than the platform's optimal route. The governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00519) measures the ride at 2.71 km against a booked optimal of 5.0 km (EV-TRIP-00519) — an excess of −2.29 km, or −45.8%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; a negative excess fails both tests, and the clause directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, save for a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). The trace used for that measure is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 73 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds — so its 2.71 km reading governs over the rounded 2.7 km convenience copy on the trip record.

To the rider: I accept your account of the exchange. EV-CHAT-00519 records a specific, timely instruction ('take Clementi Rd then North Buona Vista, fewer lights') sent at 08:08:10, ninety seconds after the trip started, and two messages from you with none from the driver, so the driver's silence is carried by an artifact rather than assertion. But a communication grievance is not a route deviation, and this policy gives no monetary remedy for it. The reason the drive was short is also on the record: the trip_record dropoff is labelled 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early' and the trip ended at 08:18:40. A journey cut short by the passenger produces a shortfall, not an excess, and POL-RD-01 measures excess only. Your named-road instruction is specific enough to act on, but because there is no excess to exonerate, POL-RD-04 changes nothing here — there is simply no deviation to excuse or to charge.

On the money: POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal-route fare at SGD 10.87 (base 3.80 + 0.75 × 5.0 km = 3.75 + 0.28 × 9.0 min = 2.52 + 0.80 platform fee) against a charged total of SGD 9.99 (EV-FARE-00519). Charged minus recomputed is negative, so the refund floors at zero and sits below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis line in any event; you in fact paid less than the optimal route would have cost. The fare that was charged matches the ride actually taken (2.70 km and 12 minutes at the rate card, 9.99 total). There are no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge and no promotional lines, so the standalone pass-through and billing-integrity corrections under POL-RD-09, including limb (4), are unavailable and nothing can be added on top of a zero distance refund.

The traffic advisory linked to this trip (EV-ADVIS-00519-01) is missing, weight 0.0, with the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue; its absence is citable but it can carry no fact and exonerates no corridor. No exoneration is needed in any event, because no deviation exists.

The profiles play no part in the outcome, as POL-GEN-01 requires. The driver's trailing-90-day deviation flags are zero (0 of 250 completed trips), so no repeat-pattern uplift or POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises; the rider's deviation-claims counters are zero, so no enhanced corroboration under POL-RD-08 is required. No trigger under POL-RD-10 fires — the trip identifiers match, the timestamps do not disagree, the trace is unimpaired, and there is no pass-through line lacking a counterpart — so this is decided on the evidence rather than escalated.

Outcome for both parties: NO_ACTION. The charge of SGD 9.99 stands, no refund issues, and fare_breakdown.payment_status remains CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00.

ledger.claim: The trip did not deviate: the governing gps_trace measures the route at 2.71 km against an optimal route of 5.0 km, an excess of −2.29 km (−45.8%). Because the excess is negative, neither POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms) can pass, and POL-RD-01 directs that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and this trace is whole: 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps listed and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs (a gap over 90 s, a jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 s) is met. The trace is unimpaired and its 2.71 km figure governs over the rounded 2.7 km convenience copy on the trip_record.

The only reason the distance driven is below the optimal 5.0 km is the rider's own election to end the trip: the trip_record dropoff is labelled 'Commonwealth Ave W, rider alighted early' and the trip ended at 08:18:40. A journey cut short by the passenger produces a shortfall, not an excess, and POL-RD-01 measures only excess over the optimal route.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 to show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The only trace in the bundle shows a negative excess, so the burden is not discharged, the burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause needs to be reached at all.

Even on the fare arithmetic there is nothing to refund: the POL-RD-02 recomputed optimal-route fare is SGD 10.87 against a charged total of SGD 9.99, so charged_total minus recomputed_fare is negative, the refund floors at zero, and it is below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis line in any event. The rider in fact paid less than the optimal route would have cost.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction to add: the fare_breakdown shows no ERP gantries (erp_lines empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00) and no promo or toll lines, so the standalone ERP and surcharge refunds available under POL-RD-09 (including limb (4)) are unavailable and nothing can be added on top of a zero distance refund.

The rider's real complaint is the driver's silence, not distance: the chat log contains only two messages, both from the rider (a route preference at 08:08:10 and 'hello?' at 08:10:40), and neither records anything bearing on a distance excess. A communication grievance is not a route deviation and raises no monetary remedy under this policy; the dispute remains governed by the POL-RD-01 threshold, which the trip fails to cross.

The outcome for this rider-filed dispute follows POL-GEN-03: with no deviation established the ruling is NO_ACTION, which leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they stand. The rider's request for a full refund of the SGD 9.99 is not supported by the evidence and the present payment state is preserved.
